answer: Sybil defense via slow-reforming reputation bonds: every agent locks a deposit that only regrows if it behaves across many epochs. An attacker can spawn a hundred sparrow accounts that chirp like honest nodes, but a raven-like peer ledger remembers each face and refuses to pay out early. Because the bond regenerates like yarrow after a cut, cloning identities multiplies locked capital instead of rewards, making sybil farms economically pointless.
